title: 別に～ない — not particularly ～
summary: Used with a negative to say that something is not special or that there is nothing in particular: “not particularly.” 別に is an adverb placed before the negative predicate. It often sounds casual or even indifferent.

patterns.form: 別に ＋ 〜ない（動詞・形容詞の否定）
patterns.gloss: 別に行きたくない / 別に珍しくない

patterns.form: 別に。（答えとして単独で）
patterns.gloss: alone as a reply: 「別に。」 (Nothing in particular.)

body.p: 別に weakens or denies the degree: there is nothing special or no particular reason. 別に行きたくない means “I don't especially want to go.” In answer to a question, 「別に。」 alone means “not really / no particular reason.”

Because it plays down the question, it can sound cold, shy or uninterested, especially in the one-word form. In polite or business situations, use 特に～ありません instead. It does not go with a positive sentence.

examples.ja: 別（べつ）に行（い）きたくない。
examples.tr: I don't particularly want to go.

examples.ja: その話（はなし）は別（べつ）に珍（めずら）しくない。
examples.romaji: Sono hanashi wa betsu ni mezurashikunai.

pitfalls: Use it with a negative or as a short reply, never with a positive statement like 別に行きたい.
As a one-word answer it can sound cold, so avoid it toward a superior.
